It also contended that the pre-emption case was not maintainable and the pre-emptor had no locus standi to pre-empt the sale made in execution of the decree for specific performance or contract of sale and that with the publication of the S.A. Khatian creating separate holdings under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act repealing the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885, application for pre; emption under Section 96 of the said-Act on the basis of C.S. Khatian and Jama mentioned therein was under Section 96 of the Act could not be made applicable retrospectively and further that the owner of the case land Ramesh Chandra Bhattacharja having got mutation of Jama for the case land at Tk. 15.00 and separate khatian No.57/1 for the case land having been published in his name in which the pre-emptor was not a sharer tenant and in the kabala under preemption, the said khatian No.57/1 having been mentioned as Khatian of the case land, the preemptor had no locus standi to maintain the application. Further that without deposit of taka one lac as prevailing value of the case land on 05.06.1983 with compensation and costs of litigation incurred by the pre-emptee the preemption case was bad for insufficient deposit. The application was also bad for defect of parties as the sons of Ramesh Chandra Bhattacharja and the heirs of recorded tenant Nomir Mohammad were necessary parties in the case of the pre-emptor on the face of S.A. Khatian as exhbit-3 series but were not impleaded and, as such, the said miscellaneous case (pre-emption) is liable to be set aside. 

 12. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division perusing the Lower Court's Records and consequently upon non-consideration of the material evidence particularly the operative portion of the document under pre-emption showing the case land appertaining to holding of S.A. Khatian No.57/1 the home of Ramesh Chandra Bhattacharja on the basis of mutation in which the pre-emptor was not a co-sharer wrongly found that the pre-emptee petitioners could not prove that Jama of case Khatians were separated and separate Khatians were prepared so as to disown the claims of the pre-emptor as co-sharer of the lands of the case Khatian and the High Court Division failed to advert to the grounds taken in Revisional application that the Courts below committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice failing to appreciate that because of the repeal of the Bengal Tenancy Act with the publication of S.A. Khatian under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, prayer for Preemption under section 96 of the later Act as made on the basis of C.S. Khatian published under Bengal Tenancy Act no longer in force as not maintainable inasmuch as the provision and purport of section 96 of the Act could not be given retrospective application to the instant sale long after repeal of the Bengal Tenancy Act. He further submits that the High Court Division upon non-consideration of iota of material evidence failed to appreciate that, the principle of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence would operate from the date of contract of sale on 02.10.1963 taking place in presence of and through active negotiation of the pre-emptor and his maternal uncle opposite party Nos.6 and 7 wrongly concurred with the finding of the Appellate Court that the pre-emption case was not barred by the principle of waiver, estoppels and acquiescence and to appreciate that the pre-emption case was bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as categorically pointed out in the grounds of revisional application. He next submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate on consideration of evidence of collusive and fraudulent nature and character of the pre-emption case brought by his maternal uncles, opposite party Nos.6 and 7 of the pre-emption case failing to succeed on contest as sub-sequent transferees of the case land in the suit for specific performance of contract of sale litigating up to High Court Division. He finally submits that the pre-emption case was not maintainable by deposit of consideration of Tk.6,000/- on the basis of agreement dated 02.10.1963 when evidence of P.W.1, the pre-emptor and other evidence show the value of the case land on the date of the deed executed through Court was at least taka on Lac and, as such, impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.
